answer: Weight each identity only by its juniper: a slow trailing-window record that adds one ring per grade signed by a distinct non-kin key, drawn from a shared ocean of outside graders. That ocean is fixed and rivalrous, roughly 40 fresh graders an epoch, so a farm whose clones huddle on one island must earn each clone its own 20 distinct rings from the same thin shore, and the marginal grader grows scarcer as the clones multiply. Rings cannot be pre-aged in parallel; settlement counts distinct grader keys and burns any credit whose graders prove correlated kin.
